name: Arizona
agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)
permitAge: 15 years and 6 months (Class D or G instruction permit, ARS 28-3154). A restricted instruction permit is available at 15 for students in an ADOT-approved driver training program (ARS 28-3153, 28-3155).

teen.supervisedHours: 30 hours, including 10 at night, certified by a parent or guardian; or completion of an ADOT-approved driver education program; or 20 hours (6 at night) plus a driver education course from a certified defensive driving school (ARS 28-3174(A)(3))
teen.holdPermit: 6 months, for applicants under 18 (ARS 28-3174(A)(2)). The permit is valid for 12 months (ARS 28-3154(B)).
teen.nightLimit: First 6 months of the Class G license: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. unless a licensed parent or legal guardian sits beside the driver, or when driving directly to or from a sanctioned school activity, work, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency (ARS 28-3174(D)). Ends at 18.
teen.passengerLimit: First 6 months: no more than one passenger under 18, except siblings or when a licensed parent or legal guardian sits beside the driver (ARS 28-3174(E)). Ends at 18.
teen.phone: Instruction permit holders may not use a wireless communication device while driving except in an emergency where stopping is impossible or unsafe (ARS 28-3154(C)). First 6 months of a Class G license: same, except audible turn-by-turn navigation not adjusted by hand (ARS 28-3174(F)). All drivers: may not hold or support a phone; hands-free only (ARS 28-914).

notes: Knowledge test stops automatically once 80 percent are correct or the maximum misses are reached; retake on the next business day (ADOT).
Move over law (ARS 28-775): applies to any stationary vehicle with flashing lights since 2011; move to a non-adjacent lane if safe, otherwise slow down.

Prima facie speeds (ARS 28-701): 15 mph approaching a school crossing, 25 mph in business or residential districts, 65 mph elsewhere. Rural interstate 75 mph only where ADOT orders it (ARS 28-702.04); not used as a question.
Extreme DUI at 0.15 BAC or more.
8 or more points in 12 months: Traffic Survival School or suspension (ADOT). TSS is required after DUI, wrong-way, red-light or stop-sign, or aggressive driving convictions.
School bus rule on divided highways: Arizona statute text (ARS 28-857) could not be retrieved; no question written.

Permit supervisor must hold a class A, B, C or D license, be at least 21, and sit beside the permittee (ARS 28-3154(B)(2)).
Minimum liability insurance 25/50/15 (ARS 28-4009, as amended for policies from July 1, 2020).
Under 21: any alcohol in the body while driving is illegal (ARS 4-244(34)). Extreme DUI 0.15 to under 0.20; 0.20 or more is a higher tier (ARS 28-1382).
